data.summary: The paper character and umbrella remain distinct, with a readable opening and rain bouncing from the canopy. The camera crops the canopy on the left, and the umbrella never shelters the nearby flower. Blue drops land directly in that flower during the ending.

observations.text: A recognizable braided paper woman watches the falling folded drops and brings both hands to the closed teal umbrella. Clothing and leaf cape retain the reference palette and paper construction.

The canopy unfolds above her and drops visibly tumble away from its surface. It stays upright above her rather than tilting toward the right-side cream flower. The push-in starts cutting the left canopy edge.

She looks toward the flower and then toward camera, retaining a separate umbrella and cape. The flower remains exposed and is visibly hit by drops, including one inside its petals in the final frame. The complete canopy and flower-sheltering requirements fail.
